subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should this issue require one complete cross-surface fallback-completion policy before closure, or should maintainers accept the embedded sessions_spawn mitigation first and track gateway loopback, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn as follow-ups?
rationale: The remaining gap is not a mechanical source edit in this issue review; it is the product and ownership boundary for fail-closed work-spawning behavior across OpenClaw and Codex-owned tools.

options.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation First
options.body: Land the embedded sessions_spawn guard when review-ready, keep this issue open, and track the other spawn-capable surfaces as explicit follow-ups.

options.title: Require One Complete Policy
options.body: Hold the candidate PR until the same fallback-completion invariant mechanically covers gateway loopback, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn or documents non-exposure.

options.title: Narrow The Contract
options.body: Define this issue as only the OpenClaw embedded sessions_spawn bug and open separate canonical issues for broader work-delegation semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation First
recommendation.body: Land the embedded sessions_spawn guard when review-ready, keep this issue open, and track the other spawn-capable surfaces as explicit follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The cross-harness review already framed the exact scope decision and Vincent has recent fallback-area history.
